Project: PRJ-LANTERN
Contributor: Tariq Al-Mansoori
Date: 2025-02-03
Location: Emirates Palace lobby cafe, Abu Dhabi
Type: Interview transcript
Source: (see filename)

CONTRIBUTOR: Farid, thanks for making the time. You left Meridian Gulf Bank in, what, late 2023?
SOURCE: November 2023, yes. Eleven years there, the last four as Head of Compliance. Before that I was at the Gulf Fintech Regulatory Office for a couple of years.
CONTRIBUTOR: So you saw both sides of the licensing process.
SOURCE: Both sides. And I still talk to Nadia Kamel in licensing every month or so. She is Deputy Director now. If you want her directly she is at n.kamel@example.ae, but go through me first.
CONTRIBUTOR: Understood. What does a payments applicant get wrong?
SOURCE: They assume the sandbox is a shortcut. It is not. The sandbox route took Baltic Pay's competitor fourteen months. The bank partnership letter is the real gate and Meridian only issues three or four a year.
CONTRIBUTOR: Who signs those?
SOURCE: Omar Bin Rashed on the retail side, but the credit committee has the veto. Omar and I were at the same school in Beirut, I am Lebanese, so I can usually get a read. My mobile is +971 50 123 4567 if you need me on the day.
CONTRIBUTOR: Any personal exposure we should know about?
SOURCE: I have a personal loan of AED 2.4m with Meridian still outstanding, so I will not be quoted on their credit decisions. My brother-in-law runs a family exchange house in Sharjah, which is why I stay well away from remittance licences.

CONTRIBUTOR NOTES
F. Haddad remains well placed. Reliability high on process, lower on anything touching Meridian's credit committee given his loan. Known to me since 2016 through the compliance forum. Next time: ask about the 2026 regulator priorities memo.
